title: Baroque 3
description: Revise concepts associated with Baroque up to Advanced Higher. These features and forms may also occur in other periods.

items.prompt: Name the general device in which one part copies an idea heard shortly before in another part; the whole melody need not be copied exactly.
A keyboard instrument whose traditional form sends air through ranks of pipes; electronic versions imitate its sustained tones.
Name the orchestral family containing violin, viola, cello and double bass.
In the Western classical stage tradition, a sung drama uses solo arias, recitative and choruses with orchestral accompaniment. Name this type of work.
A bass note is held or repeated while the chords above it change, sometimes clashing with the held note.
A major tonic chord used at the end of a piece or section in a minor key.
An important decorative instrumental line is played alongside a solo vocal melody. Name this accompanying line.
The beat grouping changes from two groups of three to three groups of two, or the other way round. The note lengths stay the same.
In a fugue, the subject is restated by the next voice, usually beginning a fifth above or a fourth below.
In a fugue, name the recurring secondary melody regularly heard alongside entries of the subject or answer.
In a fugue, a new subject entry begins before the previous one ends, so they overlap.
